text.text: The Nintendo GameCube was released in 2001 as Nintendo's sixth-generation home console. It introduced a compact optical disc format and focused on first-party games, local multiplayer, and unique hardware designs. The system featured major franchises including Super Smash Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Metroid Prime, Mario, Luigi's Mansion, Pikmin, Animal Crossing, and F-Zero. The GameCube controller became known for its distinctive layout and remains popular for competitive gaming. Nintendo also released accessories such as the Game Boy Player, allowing Game Boy, Game Boy Color, and Game Boy Advance games to be played on the console. Although it competed against the PlayStation 2 and Xbox, the GameCube developed a strong software library and continues to have an active fan community.
